title: Owner decision log
purpose: The suggestion queue on suggestions.html is 21 entries long, and a queue nobody closes becomes a backlog. This register is the single place an owner's choice is recorded so that a later agent pass can implement the chosen path without re-asking. It is the write-side of the review step: every suggestion gets a path picked, or an explicit hold.

policy.name: adopt-after-silence
policy.text: A suggestion whose recommended path is reversible, low-risk, and does not depend on a fact only an Amazon account holder can supply is treated as pre-approved: the next agent pass implements it and records what it did on this page. Everything else holds until the owner picks. This exists because the brief says no manual input is required of the owner, while also requiring that a human reviews suggestions before changes - so the review has a default outcome rather than a veto that blocks the work.
policy.scope_limit: Silence never authorises: spending money, registering a domain, contacting Amazon or a brand on the owner's behalf, publishing an Amazon-served price or star rating, changing a compliance posture, deleting another session's committed evidence, or asserting any product fact the repository has flagged as unverified. Anything in that class waits, on this page, with its reason.
policy.rule_applied: auto-adopt requires: an option letter the suggestion recommends; that option marked reversible; that option's risk 'none' or 'low'; and no blocking question in state 'unknowable'. The four tests are computed from data/suggestions.json and data/questions.json at build time, so the table on the page cannot claim a default its own data does not support.
policy.recording: An executed default is recorded in `implemented`, never in `choices`. A pass that adds a row to `choices` is inventing an owner instruction; a pass that changes data without recording it in `implemented` is the same failure in the other direction.

how_to_return_a_choice: Pick the path on decision-log.html. The page stores it in this browser so a second visit shows the same answer.
Press 'Copy decision record' (or 'Download decision-log.json') and send the text back in any session, or commit it over this file.

The next agent pass reads data/decision-log.json before it reads suggestions.html's defaults, records what it implemented, and marks the row. Anything you did not pick keeps the default this page shows today.
choices_note: Empty at publication, deliberately. An owner decision is a fact about a person's intent, and no agent session may record one on their behalf - that is the difference between a default and a fabricated instruction. Rows appear here only after a choice is actually made, and each one carries its date.

implemented.what: Computed the 'start here' triage from the registers' own blocker fields and published it on decision-log.html, above the register: each row's downstream count is the transitive size of its 'blocks' arrays across data/suggestions.json and data/questions.json, so the ranking regenerates with the registers instead of going stale (the F63/F52 defect class this repository keeps finding).
implemented.why_allowed: SG-26's own default: option A, reversible, risk low, blocked only by questions in state 'missing' rather than 'unknowable'. The standing rule on this page authorises exactly that.

implemented.what: Every outbound product CTA is now composed by the build as a canonical amazon.com/dp/<ASIN>?tag=<config tag> link, with check_special_links() failing the build on an untagged anchor, a link aimed at the short-link redirector, a tag the config never declared, or a tag whose shape violates Amazon's published XXXXX-## pattern. The supplied short links stay visible on each product page as the artefact being checked, not the destination.
implemented.why_allowed: The owner supplied the tracking ID in writing on 2026-11-17, so the value is an instruction rather than an invention; the change is reversible by deleting one config key; and it publishes no Amazon-served price, no rating and no product fact the registers have not already recorded. The scope_limit on this page forbids spending money and asserting unverified facts - neither is done: the ASINs are carried forward as candidates.

implemented.what: Added the compact call-to-action produced by the same builder to the category table, the comparison matrix's final row and the picks cards, each carrying the affiliate chip and the page-level disclosure rather than a duplicated paragraph.
implemented.why_allowed: Reversible, low-risk, no new claims: it links to the same three candidate ASINs already marketed on the product pages, and it was the row that made the tag change worth shipping.

implemented.what: Gave the two seasonal articles an explicit validity window in data/articles.json, rendered it on their pages, and added check_seasonal_expiry() so the build fails the day after a window closes until someone re-dates it against a fresh read or removes the row.
implemented.why_allowed: Amazon's policy states the removal duty in dated terms, the change adds a constraint rather than a claim, and the failure mode it prevents is a page asserting a promotion that ended. Reversible by deleting the season block, which would be a regression, not a preference.

implemented.what: Added a four-question band to the front page above the format guide, each card linking an article that answers it, and wrote the fourth guide (multi-function buying questions) that the brief listed and the article set lacked.
implemented.why_allowed: Content shape, not a commercial claim: every link in the band points at an existing sourced article, the new guide cites only manufacturer pages and manuals, and the register records the traffic argument as a judgement rather than a measured demand signal.

implemented.what: Built the page-level attribution mechanism and stopped at its door: sub_tags.assigned in data/config.json is read, validated and applied per page, and left empty. Creating the tracking IDs themselves is an action inside the owner's Amazon account.
implemented.why_allowed: The half that can be automated was done; the half that would require acting as the account holder was not, which is what the standing scope limit requires.

implemented_note: Rows are written by the agent that did the work, on the date it was done, and only for suggestions the adopt-after-silence policy covers. 2026-11-17 (arena/3093e674-zone1): five rows added, one of them a partial adoption whose remaining half is an owner action. Nothing here records an owner's choice - that column is still empty, and the two decisions waiting on it (the product-set question and the account-side attribution) are named on questions.html rather than assumed here.
